messages:
taylor wong: hit another OOM on shard-c at 01:03 UTC. kv-cache mem graph shows steady linear growth after 00:30, no obvious spikes from indexing.

maria hsiao: thanks taylor. can you attach the heap dump and current jemalloc stats?

taylor wong: uploaded heapdump to /s3/ooms/1977801234/heap.pb and jemalloc stats to /s3/ooms/1977801234/jemalloc.json. pprof top: 
```
# pprof --text kv-cache.heap.2026-03-23.pb
  36.7%  36.7%  runtime.mallocgc
  22.9%  59.6%  github.com/redwood/kv.(*Cache).insert
  10.3%  69.9%  github.com/redwood/kv.(*Segment).append
```

kevin nguyen: insert path seems to allocate many small buffers. jemalloc fragmentation metric shows arena hotness high (~0.47). could be many short-lived objects promoted, or too many distinct size-classes being used.

samir patel: alert-bot: Incident 1977801234-kv-oom-shard-c created. Priority P1. Link: https://incidents.redwood/1977801234

alert-bot: Incident 1977801234 created; assigned to eng-runtime oncall.

maria hsiao: immediate mitigation proposal (short, actionable):
- IF1: apply per-process soft memory ceiling for kv-cache (owner: kevin) - target: 12h
- IF2: enable temporary aggressive eviction policy for >128kb entries (owner: taylor) - target: 6h
- IF3: start continuous jemalloc sampling at 15s and retain 72h (owner: samir) - target: 1h
- IF4: add alert rule: cache growth >10% over 10m with sustained GC pressure (owner: maria) - target: 3h

taylor wong: will open quick PR for eviction rule, will scope to canary first. PR: #4233. plan: enable on 2% traffic then 20% if stable.

kevin nguyen: on soft ceiling - prefer soft over hard to avoid crash loops. implement with throttled evictions when usage > threshold. will add instrumentation for miss rate and p90 latency.

samir patel: starting jemalloc sampling now, forwarding metrics to /alerts/kv/jemalloc. will also run a fragmentation GC prototype in staging to compare.

maria hsiao: documenting owners in postmortem follow-up doc: https://docs.redwood/eng-runtime/kv-oom-followups. I'll create a tracking table and send calendar invite for a follow-up sync in 72 hours.

kevin nguyen: quick note: if eviction of >128kb entries causes unacceptable cache miss penalty, fallback = route reads to warmed replica (feature flag routing.kv.fallback=true). I'll add a graph for miss-rate vs latency.

taylor wong: small repro snippet I'm using to stress fragmentation on staging: 
```
for i in $(seq 1 50000); do
  size=$(( (i % 5 + 1) * 64 * 1024 ))
  curl -XPOST https://staging-kv/set -d "{\"k\":$i, \"v\":$(head -c $size /dev/urandom | base64)}"
done
```

maria hsiao: good. long-term items (to track as follow-ups):
- LT-A: introduce slab allocator / pooled arenas for hot size-classes (owner: samir+kevin) - ETA 8w
- LT-B: zero-copy serialization for large values (>64kb) to avoid unnecessary memcpy (owner: taylor) - ETA 3w
- LT-C: synthetic CI job that recreates fragmentation pattern and runs on weekly stable branch (owner: taylor) - ETA 2w
- LT-D: evaluate switching default allocator tuning (owner: kevin) - ETA 4w

kevin nguyen: added LT-D to my board. will prototype arena reuse in a spike branch first.

samir patel: staging compaction benchmark tonight. if compaction reduces fragmentation metric by >15% and doesn't regress CPU, we can promote the background compactor.

maria hsiao: please post short status updates here. I'll use this thread as canonical action tracker for the incident.

taylor wong: IF2 PR #4233 opened, request review from kevin + samir. added unit tests to simulate large-entry eviction.

alert-bot: Deployment started for PR #4233 to canary.

kevin nguyen: canary deployed at 02:40 UTC to 2% of shard-c. monitoring memory, miss-rate and p95.

samir patel: EOD staging numbers: background compaction reduced fragmentation index 0.51 -> 0.36 in microbenchmark. CPU +4%. sharing perf dashboards: /dashboards/kv/frag-bench

taylor wong: initial canary looks ok after 30m, no p95 increase, memory plateaued. promoting to 20% during morning window.

maria hsiao: thanks everyone. summary for tracking doc: IF1(kevin,12h), IF2(taylor,6h), IF3(samir,1h), IF4(maria,3h), LT-A(samir+kevin,8w), LT-B(taylor,3w), LT-C(taylor,2w), LT-D(kevin,4w). retro scheduled in 3 days. :calendar: 

kevin nguyen: no blockers from my side. will continue to monitor.

taylor wong: will post final heap diffs and CI repro artifacts here when ready.

samir patel: setting recurring weekly "kv-frag-check" reminder to capture slow regressions.

maria hsiao: closing thread for now, will re-open if new incidents or failed canary.
